claim: On cloud marketplaces Anthropic, not the cloud, is the seller of Claude: it sets the price and books the revenue; the cloud collects the money and keeps a fee.
evidence: Anthropic S-1/A: CSPs act "as collection agents"; Anthropic "is the principal and recognizes revenue on a gross basis… and establishes pricing" (pp. F-17, F-22).
counter: Amazon does not disclose how it books Bedrock-Claude; each party makes its own principal/agent judgement.

claim: Cloud marketplaces carried ~44% of Anthropic's revenue in the first nine months of 2026, down from 48% in the first half (~40% implied for Q3).
evidence: Marketplace share: FY25 47%, H1'26 48%, 9M'26 44% (S-1/A p. F-17). Q3 is our calculation from the two filings.
counter: Shares are rounded ('approximately'), so the Q3 figure has a ±1.5-point range.

claim: AWS's operating margin was 38.7% in Q3 2026 while revenue grew 39% — there is no sign in reported results that AI is wrecking AWS's economics.
evidence: AWS segment: $45,984M revenue, $17,773M operating income; margin range 32.9–39.5% over nine quarters.
counter: Segment margins can't isolate Claude or any incentive; depreciation is rising faster than revenue (+63% vs +39%) and return on segment assets fell from ~30% to ~19%.

claim: About $67B of Amazon's nine-month 2026 pre-tax income (~46%) came from Anthropic mark-ups — outside AWS's operating profit. Amazon carries $238.7B of Anthropic investments for ~$18B of cash invested.
evidence: Amazon 10-Q Q3 2026, Notes 1–2 (AFS notes $146.2B; preferred $92.5B; $140.3B pre-tax gain in AOCI).
counter: Marks are non-cash and valuation-dependent; they say nothing about AWS's operating returns.

claim: OpenAI is one of Microsoft's largest customers: $24.1B of Microsoft revenue in FY26 and $10.0B (10.8% of revenue) in the September 2026 quarter.
evidence: Microsoft related-party disclosure (10-K FY26 Note 1; 10-Q Sep 2026 Note 1), 'inclusive of revenue-sharing payments'.
counter: Revenue-share receipts are mixed in; the split between Azure consumption and revenue share is not disclosed.

claim: Microsoft Cloud's gross margin fell from 71% to 66% in two years; Microsoft blamed 'scaling our AI infrastructure' every quarter to March 2026.
evidence: Microsoft 10-Q/10-K MD&A, FY25 Q1–FY26 Q3; from FY26 Q4 the driver changed to 'sales mix shift to Azure'.
counter: Operating margin held at ~50–53% in the relevant segment; AI revenue adds little selling cost.

claim: Google Cloud's 36% margin does not include Gemini's development cost, which Alphabet books centrally ($24.7B over the last four quarters, +81%).
evidence: Alphabet segment note: 'Alphabet-level activities' carry AI model development. Charging Cloud its 24% revenue share of that cost takes the Q3 margin to ~30%.
counter: Gemini also powers Search, Workspace and Android; charging all of it to Cloud would overstate Cloud's cost.

claim: Alphabet's 2026 profits also lean on stake mark-ups: nine-month equity gains ($127.3B) exceeded operating income ($121.0B), and free cash flow was negative in Q2 and Q3.
evidence: Alphabet 10-Q Q3 2026 OI&E note; FCF −$5.9B (Q2), −$9.1B (Q3).
counter: Negative FCF reflects a deliberate capex surge backed by a $561B backlog.

claim: Anthropic has promised at least $110B to AWS, $121.3B to Google Cloud and $47.2B to Azure — take-or-pay.
evidence: S-1/A Contractual Obligations (pp. 173–176); 424B4 update for Azure.
counter: Part of Anthropic's total commitments ($186.2B) is contingent or terminable; the cloud-specific minimums are non-cancelable except for breach.

claim: A one-time 35% credit is worth about 10% to a growing customer over three years and about 6% over five — it is not a 35% price cut.
evidence: Model: credits received ÷ total list spend.
assumptions: AI spend grows 30% a year; 85% chance the workload stays each year.
counter: For a customer that doesn't grow or churns early, the one-time credit is worth more.

claim: For AWS, a one-time or MAP-style 35% incentive on Claude pays back in roughly 13–17 months — if it wins a workload AWS would otherwise lose.
evidence: Model, AI line only, base case.
calc: Year-1 cost ≈ $28 per $100 (35% × 80¢ per credit dollar) against a ~$25 slice that grows with usage.
assumptions: 30% fee; credits cost the cloud 80¢ per $1 (16.5 months at $1); 30% growth; 85% retention.
counter: If the customer would have come anyway, the incentive is a pure transfer — it needs to lift AWS's win odds by ~31% of the base rate to pay.

claim: A permanent 35% discount on Claude loses money for AWS on the Claude line alone — but roughly breaks even with modest extra cloud business or Amazon's equity upside.
evidence: Model: 5-year value −$24 per $100 (AI only), +$44 with base adjacency.
calc: Break-even needs ~$5–12 of incremental non-AI gross profit per $100 of AI a year, or ~8% of the subsidized usage to be new revenue for Anthropic.
assumptions: Base adjacency $0.20 incremental per $1 at 70% gross margin; Amazon stake ~23%, ~14× run-rate revenue.
counter: Adjacent attach is not disclosed by any cloud; equity gains are non-cash and only count for genuinely new usage.

claim: For Google, matching a 35% one-time incentive pays only if it lifts our win odds by at least ~8% of the base rate on Gemini — but ~31% on Claude resold through Vertex.
evidence: Model: required lift = base win rate × (value without − value with) ÷ value with.
assumptions: Base case; one-time incentive; five-year value.
counter: Customers choose models, not margins — a Gemini match can't win a workload that needs Claude.

claim: AI revenue at all three clouds is partly vendor-financed: each invests in model makers that commit to spend on it.
evidence: Amazon: $18B into Anthropic, $50B into OpenAI; Microsoft: OpenAI bills ≈ OpenAI's revenue; Google: ~$23B into Anthropic plus $48B of credit backstops.
counter: These are disclosed, contractual arrangements — not evidence of improper accounting.

claim: Google is at least as dependent on Anthropic as AWS: ≥21.6% of Google Cloud's backlog vs ~19% of AWS's.
evidence: Anthropic minimums (≥$121.3B Google, ≥$110B AWS) vs backlog ($560.8B, $578B).
counter: Commitments run to different end dates than backlog; the excluded $125–150B of extra TPUs could raise Google's share.

claim: Per dollar, Google keeps more of a Gemini sale (~$74 of $100, ~$51 after model cost) than AWS keeps of a Claude sale (~$25).
evidence: Model waterfall; agent vs principal structure from the S-1/A.
assumptions: Gemini serving 10% of list on TPUs; 2.5% cost of capital; 25% model-development charge (anchors 6–58%).
counter: Google's own 50% introductory Gemini pricing leaves ~$1 per $100 in year one after model cost — Google subsidizes too.

claim: When a one-time credit ends, the customer's bill for the same usage rises ~54–64% — unless list prices keep falling, in which case the jump is ~0–6%.
evidence: Model: 1 ÷ (1 − 0.35) − 1 = 54%; with a 10% discount 64%; with 35% annual list-price cuts ~0–6%.
counter: Falling prices can hide the cliff entirely; the real cost is the customer forgoing a year of price-cut savings.

claim: Clouds keep roughly $12–30 of each $100 of Claude they resell (central ~$25), before incentives.
evidence: Anthropic's channel-partner fees ÷ marketplace revenue: ~16% (FY2025), 33–36% (9M 2026), ~32% (Q3 2026); Reuters made the same calculation for 2025.
assumptions: All channel-partner fees go to clouds and pay for distribution, not serving.
counter: Fees may include SIs and data platforms, may pay the cloud for serving (pool then ~$13–16), and the 2026 jump may reflect a restructured deal.

claim: AWS is offering ~35% incentives on Anthropic workloads.
evidence: Field observation. Claude on Bedrock is MAP-eligible; MAP credits are a plan-specific % of spend growth, reported ~25%. No public source shows 35% or an Anthropic-specific rate.
counter: 35% is plausible as a stacked deal (MAP + Anthropic private-offer discount + partner funding) — ask who funds each piece.
source: AWS MAP terms (via search extracts); field reports

claim: Reselling third-party models is structurally lower-margin per dollar than selling your own.
evidence: Arithmetic of the agent structure (S-1/A); AWS management says AI margins are 'still lower' than core.
counter: AWS also earns take-or-pay compute, Trainium margin and equity gains; reported results don't show the per-dollar gap hurting it.

claim: Anthropic is steering business to its direct channel and renegotiating cloud terms.
evidence: Marketplace share fell 48% → ~40%; S-1/A cites 'changes in the terms of our channel partner distribution arrangements'; 'Claude Platform on AWS' launched May 2026.
counter: The Q3 fee range overlaps 9M; the direction of the fee since Q3 cannot be determined.

claim: Since April 2026 Microsoft sells OpenAI models royalty-free, so Azure OpenAI is closer to a first-party product than to Bedrock's Claude resale.
evidence: April 27, 2026 amendment; CFO: 'royalty free with the elimination of our rev share to them'.
counter: The licence is non-exclusive and ends in 2032; OpenAI can sell on any cloud, including AWS.
source: Microsoft blog and FY26 Q3 earnings call

claim: "AWS's and Microsoft's AI subsidy model is unsustainable."
evidence: Not supported: reported cloud margins are high and rising; time-limited incentives pay back in ~1–1.5 years under base assumptions; Microsoft resells OpenAI royalty-free.
counter: Holds only for permanent, fully cloud-funded discounts on usage the cloud would have won anyway.

claim: "AWS loses money on AI" / "Bedrock is unprofitable."
evidence: Contradicted: AWS margin 38.7%; management says AI margins are improving; unverified analyst reports say Bedrock lifts AWS's margin.

claim: "Circular AI investments are fake revenue" or accounting tricks.
evidence: No evidence of misconduct; the arrangements are disclosed and contractual. The fair point is concentration and vendor financing (see the defensible-math claims).

claim: "AWS gives Anthropic customers 35% off, permanently."
evidence: No public evidence; MAP credits are growth-based and time-limited; AWS commit discounts reportedly don't apply to Claude.
counter: Individual deals may be richer than policy — verify each.

claim: "Gemini is more profitable than Claude on AWS" / "vertical integration guarantees Google wins on cost."
evidence: Unprovable from outside: Gemini's development cost and revenue are not disclosed; Gemini holds ~9% of enterprise API spend (survey) vs Anthropic's 55%.
counter: Per-dollar retention is higher on Gemini — say that instead (claim c16).

claim: "Microsoft subsidizes OpenAI with below-cost Azure pricing."
evidence: No evidence of below-list pricing; Microsoft's exposure is concentration and credit risk in a customer funded by outside capital.
